messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] pcountOpen for annual species
parts:
Hi Doug,

I'm afraid I don't have any time right now to work on this right now, but I suggest that you consider using the dynamics = 'trend' option, or switching to BUGS. 

Richard


On Mon, Sep 16, 2013 at 10:34 AM, Doug Leasure <doug.l...@gmail.com> wrote:
Thanks Richard,
Is this on the agenda for future updates to unmarked?  Seems like an easy fix that would make the model applicable to many more species.

Do you have other suggestions for modeling multi-season counts of an annual species using the robust sampling design (5 primary periods, 3 secondary periods)?  I want to include multiple years in a single model to better capture the range of variation in weather conditions that affect detectability.  The Dail & Madsen model estimates omega at values much too high to be realistic for this annual species (endangered American burying beetle, Nicrophorus americanus).  It would be perfect if I  could fix omega at 0 instead of 1.  

If I understand correctly, your model (Chandler et al. 2011) is not meant for multi-year data open to inter-annual demographics.  The model of Kery et al. (2009) seems appropriate but I'm unaware of any implementation of this model in Unmarked.  

Any suggestions?

Thanks for your help!
-Doug Leasure

On Friday, August 30, 2013 8:22:29 AM UTC-5, Richard Chandler wrote:

Richard
